author: TEDx Talks
description:
It sounds like a joke set up: I ordered a book called 'Life Without Plastic' online. It arrived wrapped in plastic. That paradoxical punchline sent one man on an assignment for The New York Times to spend one full day without touching plastic. He barely survived. Instead, he discovered that plastic is not just inconvenient to avoid. It is structurally embedded in nearly every object, material, and system we rely on daily. This funny and relatable talk makes the case that while personal habit change matters, the plastic crisis will not be solved by individual willpower alone. It requires the scale of institutional, corporate, and policy-level action that treats plastic pollution as the systemic problem it is.

title: Why quitting plastic is nearly impossible (and what actually works) | AJ Jacobs | TEDxBoston
